Clock Sanctuary

A sound-only meditation space built around grandfather clocks, with binaural and isochronic tones, mood presets and a journey with several holding points. Use headphones for the binaural tones. Nothing plays until you tap Start.

Play

Mood presets

One tap sets up the binaural tones for a mood, with carriers tuned to blend as a chord. It replaces your current binaural tones but leaves clocks and isochronic tones alone. You can edit everything afterwards. Relaxation sound design, not medical treatment.

Clocks

Each clock is a seamless loop. Turn on as many as you like.

Hour strike

The strike from W I M's grandfather clock recording. It is off unless you choose when it plays. The strike lasts about half a minute.

Binaural tones

Each binaural tone plays a slightly different pitch in each ear; the difference is the beat. Headphones are needed, as speakers mix the two ears together. Up to ten tones.

    Isochronic tones

    An isochronic tone is one pitch that pulses on and off at the beat rate. It works on speakers as well as headphones. Up to ten tones.

      Journey

      A journey moves the beat of every tone that is on through a list of stages. Each stage glides or steps to a new beat, then holds there for as long as you choose, so you can pause at several points on the way down and on the way back up.

        Lock screen advisory

        Live tones and clocks run inside Safari. On iPhone they usually stop or pause when the screen locks or you switch to another app, and the journey pauses with them. For now, keep Safari open with the screen on, perhaps with Auto-Lock set longer and the brightness turned down. The experimental setting above may keep sound going when locked on some iOS versions, but this has not been tested on your iPhone yet, so please don't rely on it for sleep. A lock-screen track you can play like music is planned for a later version.

        Help

        Quick start

        1. Put on headphones.
        2. Tap a mood preset, or leave the default: the long ticking clock and one gentle binaural tone.
        3. Tap Start. Sound fades in over a few seconds.
        4. Flick by heading to reach any section. Changes apply straight away while playing.

        If you hear nothing

        Check the volume buttons and the master volume. If the sound mode is Mix with other apps, the silent switch mutes the page, so turn silent mode off or choose the first sound mode. If iOS paused the sound, tap Start again.

        An honest note on brainwave tones

        The band names, delta, theta, alpha and beta, are conventional labels. Research on whether binaural or isochronic beats change brain states is mixed and weak. Treat the tones as relaxation sound design that some people enjoy, not as medical treatment, and not as a treatment for anxiety. Ten beats at once blur together into one rich chord of pulses. If any tone feels uncomfortable, stop. People with epilepsy should take medical advice before using pulsing sound.

        About ten layers

        Ten binaural and ten isochronic tones at once is fine for an iPhone 11. The app automatically lowers each tone as you add more, and a limiter guards against distortion, so the overall loudness stays about the same.

        Saving

        Your settings are saved on this iPhone in Safari, and come back next time you open the page.
